_readme: Project architecture rules for the jikan-rest API (read-only PHP/Laravel JSON API). Sections for audits that describe client-UI or FormRequest/route-model-binding conventions (errorHandling, contractHeaders, formRequestValidation, routeModelBinding) are deliberately absent: this API validates through spatie Data DTOs, binds ids through a mediator, and has no UI, so those audits refuse ('could not check') instead of reporting a vacuous zero. Route audits parse the class-based, named route spelling used in routes/web.v4.php.

layerBoundaries._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_layer_boundaries.py. Every rule in rules[] is enforced (an earlier version read rules[0] only); baseline is the recorded oracle the ratchet compares against. On a PHP project mustNotImport may name a namespace root (App\Http\) or a repo-rooted path — both compare by prefix, and one rule may ban both.

rules.label: HTTP layer must not import Service layer
Service layer must not import HTTP layer

apiConsistency._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_api_consistency.py. checks: each of the four (loadBearingCopy, hardBakedCopy, authoredSemantics, vocabulary) is true or {"enabled": false, "why": "..."} — an unconfigured check refuses rather than passes. authoredSemantics is a client-UI-provenance check (an interaction must author a named semantics node); on a server-side tree the interaction surface lives in the client app, so turn it off with a why rather than letting every route report as an unnamed interaction. vocabularyRules: this project's own naming rules, [{message, classPattern?, classNotPattern?, has, hasNot?}] — a class whose name matches, whose members all match has, and whose members match none of hasNot is a finding; vocabulary on with zero rules refuses rather than sweeping clean.

authoredSemantics.why: server-side tree; interaction surfaces live in the client app

vocabularyRules.message: uses fetch, where the codebase names this find
uses find, where the codebase names this fetch

routeCoverage._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_route_coverage.php. routesGlob: glob for route files. actionPattern: regex to extract controller and method from a class-based route, [Controller::class, 'method']. controllerDirs: directories to scan for controllers.

cacheTtlCoverage._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_cache_ttl_coverage.php. routesGlob: glob for route files. actionPattern: regex to extract the route name (the TTL key) from ->name('v4.<resource>.<action>'). ttlConfigGlob: glob for TTL config file. ttlKeyPattern: regex to extract the same key from the TTL config.

endpointParity._comment: verifies route/controller-action parity for class-based routes ([Controller::class, method]); no extra config needed

rateLimit._comment: public v4 API is globally throttled via the v4 group + RateLimiter::for('v4')

toolchainGates._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_toolchain_gates.py. Declares the manifest(s) and runner(s) that define the project's toolchain, so test-suite declarations and runner directories cannot silently drift.

testNetworkCoupling._comment: Consumed by bin/audit_test_network_coupling.py. Tests must never reach myanimelist.net: Tests\TestCase::createApplication() replaces the parser's HTTP client with a mock that throws CustomTestException on any request. A host-referencing test therefore counts as safe when it extends that TestCase (or builds its own mock); a test constructing a real client is a finding.
